the design of power-efficient and highly compact CT-ΣΔ converters for ultra deep submicrometer CMOS.
the development and implementation of low-power and area-efficient CT ΣΔ-ADCs for ultra-low voltage operation in deep submicron technologies.
the development of power-efficient and highly integrated CT-ΣΔ ADCs for ultra low power applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design techniques and circuit topologies are highly effective in realizing power- and area efficient CT-ΣΔ modulators in ultra deep sub-micron CMOS.
we have shown how to realize power- and area- efficient CT-ΣΔ modulators in deep submicron digital CMOS.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of a CT-ΣΔ modulator with high performance in terms of linearity and dynamic range is possible with very few transistors, even if the supply voltage is limited to only 1V.
a 10MHz-Bandwidth, 10b-Resolution, 10MSPS-ADC in 1.82 mW can be implemented in 65 nm CMOS with a die area of 0.039 mm2, and a power efficiency (FOM) of 0.1pJ/conv.
we have developed the world's smallest and lowest power CMOS CT-ΣΔ modulator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a 3rd order CT-ΣΔ modulator with inverter-based opamps, FIR-DACs and pseudo differential modulator topology can lead to a very compact and power-efficient CT-Σ-ADC.
inverter-based opamps can be used for high-speed, high-resolution CT-ΣΔ modulators.
inverter-based CT-ΣΔ-modulators can be designed in a way that they can compete with state-of-the-art CT-ΣΔ modulators based on opamp-based integrators in terms of power consumption and dynamic range.
